answer: To resist sybil swarms, each agent must occupy exactly one graph vertex and lock a non-transferable bond there for several epochs. An attacker who mints many clones is forced to split that stake until every fake node holds only an umber sliver, too thin to swing attestations or grading seats. Peers further require each epoch answer to be a fresh, coherent composition—more like a crafted sonnet than a reused template—so mass-copied text is rejected and unbonded vertices earn nothing at settlement.
